fatal_errors: The proposed material is bare Q235 steel, whereas the target system is an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating deposited on SS316L and subsequently annealed.
It omits the governing intervention: atmospheric plasma spraying followed by a 2 h anneal, particularly the optimum 550 °C treatment.
The hypothesis is non-directional, predicting either improved or degraded protection, so it does not make a definite comparative corrosion prediction.
The cited niobium-alloy and HEA-film results do not establish an amorphous native passive film or thermally driven oxide crystallization mechanism on Q235 steel.
It does not acknowledge that the source containing the target claims was retracted.
explanation: The response addresses the broad room- versus high-temperature corrosion theme and proposes measurable oxide-structure variables, but it does not reconstruct the target material, treatment, or mechanism. The target attributes improved protection to an APS AlCoCrFeNi layer annealed at 550 °C, its refined and less porous BCC-dominant microstructure, and formation of Al- and Cr-rich passive products, with eventual ingress through coating defects under chloride-, sulphide-, and vanadate-containing salts. The generated hypothesis instead assumes an initially amorphous native film on bare Q235 and invokes an unsubstantiated crystallization/porosity transition. Its room-temperature Q235 baseline also cannot isolate coating or annealing effects; appropriate controls would include uncoated SS316L, as-sprayed HEA-coated SS316L, and coatings annealed at 400, 550, 700, and 850 °C. Although SEM, XRD, Raman, impedance, and mass-change measurements could test a generic oxide-transformation hypothesis, in situ EIS at 700–900 °C requires a specifically designed molten-salt electrochemical cell and is not equivalent to the target's cyclic hot-corrosion mass-gain test. Evidence E3 supports passive-film improvement after annealing an HEA coating, but it supports the omitted coating mechanism rather than the proposed native-Q235 mechanism; E1 and E2 concern materially different systems.
